claim: Cells expressing R172K mutant IDH2 did not display isocitrate-dependent NADPH production above vector control levels.
source: We found that cells expressing R172K mutant IDH2 did not display isocitrate-dependent NADPH production above vector control levels, in contrast to the increased production observed with wild-type IDH2.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from the replication study showing OD340 measurements for R172K mutant IDH2 and vector control.

claim: Wild-type IDH2 showed increased isocitrate-dependent NADPH production compared to R172K mutant IDH2.
source: We found that cells expressing R172K mutant IDH2 did not display isocitrate-dependent NADPH production above vector control levels, in contrast to the increased production observed with wild-type IDH2.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data comparing wild-type and mutant IDH2 NADPH production.

claim: Expression of R172K mutant IDH2 resulted in increased alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent consumption of NADPH compared to wild-type IDH2 or vector control.
source: Conversely, expression of R172K mutant IDH2 resulted in increased alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent consumption of NADPH compared to wild-type IDH2 or vector control.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing NADPH consumption measurements.

claim: The replication results for NADPH production and consumption are similar to those reported in the original study (Figure 2; Ward et al., 2010).

evidence: The claim compares replication results to the original study by citation.

claim: Expression of R172K mutant IDH2 resulted in increased 2HG levels within cells compared to the background levels observed in wild-type IDH2 and vector control.
source: Further, expression of R172K mutant IDH2 resulted in increased 2HG levels within cells compared to the background levels observed in wild-type IDH2 and vector control, similar to the original study (Figure 3D; Ward et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from GC-MS analysis of intracellular metabolites.

claim: The increased 2HG levels in R172K mutant IDH2 expressing cells are similar to the original study (Figure 3D; Ward et al., 2010).

claim: In primary human AML samples, the 2HG levels observed in samples with mutant IDH1 or IDH2 status were higher than those observed in samples without an IDH mutation.
source: In primary human AML samples, the 2HG levels observed in samples with mutant IDH1 or IDH2 status were higher than those observed in samples without an IDH mutation, similar to what was observed in the original study (Figure 5C; Ward et al., 2010).

claim: The 2HG levels in AML samples with IDH mutations are similar to what was observed in the original study (Figure 5C; Ward et al., 2010).

claim: Ward et al. (2010) demonstrated that a shared feature of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutations identified in gliomas and acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is the acquisition of a neomorphic enzyme activity.
source: In 2010, Ward et al. demonstrated that a shared feature of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutations identified in gliomas and acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is the acquisition of a neomorphic enzyme activity.
evidence: The claim references findings from the Ward et al. 2010 study.

claim: Cancer-associated IDH1 mutations resulted in increased production of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate (2HG) (Dang et al., 2009).
source: This study built upon a previous study demonstrating cancer-associated IDH1 mutations resulted in increased production of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate (2HG) (Dang et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim references findings from Dang et al. 2009 study.

claim: The cancer-associated IDH2 R172 mutation was demonstrated to be deficient in isocitrate-dependent NADPH production (Yan et al., 2009; Ward et al., 2010).
source: Similar to the IDH1 R132 mutation, the cancer-associated IDH2 R172 mutation was demonstrated to be deficient in isocitrate-dependent NADPH production (Yan et al., 2009; Ward et al., 2010), while acquiring a gain of function for alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent NADPH consumption that resulted in the production of 2HG (Ward et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim references findings from Yan et al. 2009 and Ward et al. 2010 studies.

claim: The cancer-associated IDH2 R172 mutation acquired a gain of function for alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent NADPH consumption that resulted in the production of 2HG (Ward et al., 2010).

evidence: The claim references findings from Ward et al. 2010 study.

claim: 2HG was reported to be detectable in AML patient samples and predictive of IDH mutational status (Ward et al., 2010).
